meta.title: The New Bracelet
meta.textType: story: the theme and the parts

paragraphs: On Sunday, Lily and Tom visited Grandma and Grandpa in Green Hill. Grandma was in the kitchen, and the oven was warm. She wanted to bake bread for lunch. Lily saw a small box on the table. Inside the box was Grandma's old red bracelet, and it was broken. "I have had it for thirty years," said Grandma. "The string is too thin now." Lily felt sorry for her. Then she had an idea.

"Grandma, I will make you a new bracelet," said Lily. "That is a surprising idea," said Grandma with a smile. "Can you really do it?" asked Tom. "I hope so," said Lily. She had a bag of red and white beads in her backpack. Grandpa gave her some very thin string from his box. Lily worked for a long time. But the bracelet was too small, and it did not fit Grandma's hand.

Lily made a second bracelet, and this time it was wide enough. Then the string broke, and the beads ran across the floor. Tom helped her to pick them up. "It is surprising how hard this is," said Lily. "I want to stop." Grandpa sat next to her and took out his old driving license. "I was born in this village, and I got this license long ago," he said. "But I failed my driving test two times." "Did you stop?" asked Lily. "No, I did not," said Grandpa.

"Try again with a strong string," he said. He went to his fishing box and found a green string. The string was strong, and it was not too thick. Lily measured Grandma's hand with it. Then she put the beads on the string, and Tom held the end. After an hour, the bracelet was ready. The bread came out of the oven at the same time. The smell of fresh bread filled the kitchen.

Lily gave the bracelet to Grandma. Grandma put it on her hand and looked at it for a long time. "It is lovely," she said. "I like it especially because you made it." "Now it is the best bracelet in the village," said Grandpa. Everyone ate warm bread with butter. Lily smiled at her red and white bracelet on Grandma's hand. A gift is best when you do not give up.
text.summary: Lily wants to make a new bracelet for Grandma. The first two bracelets do not work, but Grandpa tells Lily not to give up, and the third one is strong.

sentences.text: On Sunday, Lily and Tom visited Grandma and Grandpa in Green Hill.
Grandma was in the kitchen, and the oven was warm.
She wanted to bake bread for lunch.
Lily saw a small box on the table.
Inside the box was Grandma's old red bracelet, and it was broken.
"I have had it for thirty years," said Grandma.
"The string is too thin now."
Lily felt sorry for her.
Then she had an idea.
"Grandma, I will make you a new bracelet," said Lily.
"That is a surprising idea," said Grandma with a smile.
"Can you really do it?" asked Tom.
"I hope so," said Lily.
She had a bag of red and white beads in her backpack.
Grandpa gave her some very thin string from his box.
Lily worked for a long time.
But the bracelet was too small, and it did not fit Grandma's hand.
Lily made a second bracelet, and this time it was wide enough.
Then the string broke, and the beads ran across the floor.
Tom helped her to pick them up.
"It is surprising how hard this is," said Lily.
"I want to stop."
Grandpa sat next to her and took out his old driving license.
"I was born in this village, and I got this license long ago," he said.
"But I failed my driving test two times."
"Did you stop?" asked Lily.
"No, I did not," said Grandpa.
"Try again with a strong string," he said.
He went to his fishing box and found a green string.
The string was strong, and it was not too thick.
Lily measured Grandma's hand with it.
Then she put the beads on the string, and Tom held the end.
After an hour, the bracelet was ready.
The bread came out of the oven at the same time.
The smell of fresh bread filled the kitchen.
Lily gave the bracelet to Grandma.
Grandma put it on her hand and looked at it for a long time.
"It is lovely," she said.
"I like it especially because you made it."
"Now it is the best bracelet in the village," said Grandpa.
Everyone ate warm bread with butter.
Lily smiled at her red and white bracelet on Grandma's hand.
A gift is best when you do not give up.
